facts: "The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde" is a novella by Robert Louis Stevenson.
The eBook was released on June 27, 2008.
The novella consists of nine chapters.
The murder of Carew is one of the incidents involving Mr. Hyde.
Mr. Utterson regularly takes Sunday walks with Richard Enfield.
Hyde trampled a young girl and then walked away.
Hyde produced a large cheque signed by a well-known, respectable man.
Utterson knows the identity of the cheque's drawer.
Mr. Utterson reviews Dr. Jekyll's will, which bequeaths all of Jekyll's possessions to Edward Hyde.
Dr. Lanyon has not seen Dr. Jekyll in over ten years.
Utterson begins nightly vigils outside Jekyll's house.
Hyde has a key to the laboratory and possesses Jekyll's complete trust.
Mr. Utterson speaks privately with Dr. Jekyll about his will during a dinner at Jekyll's home.
Dr. Jekyll's will leaves his estate to Mr. Hyde.
Jekyll becomes distressed when Utterson mentions disturbing things about Hyde.
Utterson agrees to ensure Hyde receives fair treatment if something happens to Jekyll.
Sir Danvers Carew was murdered in October.
Mr. Hyde attacked an elderly gentleman with a cane.
The murder weapon was identified as a broken stick given to Henry Jekyll by Mr. Utterson.
Hyde's residence was found ransacked with burned papers and the other half of the murder stick.
Mr. Utterson visits Dr. Jekyll at his laboratory.
Sir Danvers Carew was murdered.
Jekyll received a letter from Edward Hyde.
Mr. Guest identifies the handwriting in the letter as nearly identical to Jekyll's own.
Dr. Jekyll initially appears to recover and resume a normal social life after Sir Danvers Carew's murder.
Lawyer Utterson visits Dr. Lanyon on January 15th and finds him gravely ill.
Dr. Lanyon refuses to discuss Jekyll and declares him "dead."
Lanyon dies within a fortnight, leaving Utterson a sealed envelope to be opened only after Jekyll's death or disappearance.
Mr. Utterson and his cousin Mr. Enfield encounter Dr. Jekyll at a window of his residence.
Dr. Jekyll declines to take a walk with Mr. Utterson and Mr. Enfield.
Dr. Jekyll's expression transforms into one of absolute terror and despair before he closes the window.
Utterson prays for forgiveness after leaving the court with Mr. Enfield.
Butler Poole visits lawyer Utterson with concerns about Dr. Jekyll.
Utterson and Poole find Edward Hyde's dead body in Jekyll's cabinet.
A note on Jekyll's desk indicates he is alive but has disappeared.
Utterson plans to examine documents from Lanyon and Jekyll before midnight.
Dr. Lanyon receives a letter from Dr. Jekyll requesting the retrieval of a drawer from Jekyll's locked cabinet.
Lanyon delivers the drawer to a mysterious messenger at midnight.
The stranger who arrives at midnight transforms into Dr. Jekyll after drinking a concoction.
Lanyon is left physically and mentally broken after witnessing Jekyll's transformation and confession.
Dr. Jekyll develops a scientific potion that separates his dual nature into two entities.
Edward Hyde commits an unprovoked murder.
Hyde retrieves the antidote drug through Dr. Lanyon.
Dr. Jekyll loses control as Hyde grows stronger and more dominant.
